name: Leg Extension
summary: A machine isolation exercise for the quadriceps that lets you load the front of the thigh directly with little help from other muscles.
setup: Adjust the seat so your knees line up with the machine's pivot point and your back is supported.
Set the pad on your lower shins just above the ankles.
Adjust the back pad so the edge of the seat sits a few finger widths behind your knees.
Hold the handles and choose a weight you can control.
execution: Extend your knees to lift the pad until your legs are almost straight.
Squeeze your quads for a moment at the top.
Lower the pad slowly, taking about two to three seconds, until your knees are bent to roughly 90 degrees.
Keep your hips in the seat and avoid swinging the weight.
Repeat for the set and lower the weight stack gently.
cues: Squeeze the quads at the top
mistakes: Swinging the weight with momentum: reduce the load and use a controlled tempo.
Hips lifting out of the seat as you reach the top: lower the weight and hold the handles or re-set the back pad.
Cutting the range short: use the full range you can control.
Slamming the weight stack at the bottom: lower slowly and stop short of resting the stack.
